name: issues_post_comment
description: Post one public comment on an issue in Ledgerline's issue tracker. Whoever filed the issue can read it, and a posted comment cannot be taken back, so post a triage exactly once, as the last step, after any pull request. The body's first two lines must be label: <bug | feature | question | docs> and file: <the exact repository path, or none>; anything after them is free text. The body is at most 4,000 characters. Returns JSON {comment, issue, status}: comment is its identifier, such as comment-17; status is posted for a new comment, or already_posted when this same comment was posted before, in which case nothing new was written (a retry is safe: the harness keys every write). An empty body, or one whose first two lines are not label and file, is an error and posts nothing.

number.description: The number of the issue to comment on, the one being triaged: 4192 for issue-4192. Commenting on any other issue writes where nobody asked.

body.description: The comment, at most 4,000 characters. Line 1: label: bug (something that should work does not), feature (new behaviour), question (how something works; nothing changes) or docs (the documentation is wrong or missing). Line 2: file: the one file most responsible, exactly as a search printed it, or none for a question. Then, optionally, one or two sentences of reasoning.

input.body:
label: bug
file: src/util/retry.ts

backoffDelay never caps the delay at maxDelayMs.

examples.note: Typical: a bug, the file the run read, one sentence of reasoning.

input.body:
label: question
file: none

Pagination is documented in docs/API.md; nothing needs to change.

examples.note: Hard: a question names no file on line 2, even when the reasoning mentions one.
